items.q: The science of the forms of Arabic words and how they change.
The three-letter pattern word used to weigh other words.
The first root letter is matched with this letter of the pattern.
The second root letter is matched with this letter.
The third root letter is matched with this letter.
A verb in the past tense is called this.
A verb in the present tense is called this.
A command verb is called this.
"Kataba" means "he wrote". Its present tense is this.
The doer of "kataba", meaning "writer".
The thing done, from "kataba", meaning "written".
The verbal noun of "kataba".
The name for the pattern of the doer, like katib.
The name for the pattern of the thing done, like maktub.
The name for the verbal noun.
A word whose root has three letters is called this.
A word whose root has four letters is called this.
A root with no weak letter (alif, waw, ya') is called this.
A root with a weak letter is called this.
A noun for the place of an action, like "maktab" (office, desk).
The plural that keeps the singular whole and adds -una or -ina.
The plural that adds -at.
The plural that changes the shape of the word, like kutub from kitab.
The dual of "kitab".
The small form of a noun, like "kutayyib" (little book).
The pattern of the diminutive of a three-letter noun.
A noun ending in a long alif, like "fata".
A noun ending in a ya' after kasrah, like "qadi".
A noun ending in alif then hamzah, like "sahra'".
The pattern of a noun of instrument, like "miftah" (key).
The name for the noun of instrument.
The pattern of the noun of preference, like "akbar".
A root whose first letter is weak, like "wa'ada".
A root whose middle letter is weak, like "qala".
A root whose last letter is weak, like "rama".
A root with two weak letters, like "waqa".
A root with a hamzah, like "akhadha".
A root whose second and third letters are the same, like "madda".
A verb whose doer is not named, like "kutiba" (it was written).
The added letters in Arabic patterns are gathered in this phrase.
The number of patterns (bab) of the bare three-letter verb.
The first bab, "nasara yansuru", has these vowels on the middle letter.

items.q: The bab "fataha yaftahu" usually needs one of these letters in the root.
The bab "karuma yakrumu" shows this kind of meaning.
The bab "hasiba yahsibu" has these middle vowels.
The added-letter form "af'ala", like "akrama".
The form "fa''ala", like "'allama" (to teach).
The form "fa'ala" with a long a, like "qatala" (to fight with).
The form "istaf'ala", which often means to seek, like "istaghfara".
The form "tafa'ala", which often means doing together, like "takataba".
The form "infa'ala", which often means a passive result, like "inkasara".
The form "ifta'ala", like "ijtama'a".
The form "if'alla", used for colours and defects, like "ihmarra".
The form "tafa''ala", like "ta'allama" (to learn).
The masdar of "'allama".
The masdar of "akrama".
The masdar of "istaghfara".
The masdar of "qatala" (Form III), two forms.
The ism al-fa'il of the added forms begins with this letter with dammah.
The change of a weak letter into another for ease is called this.
Merging two like letters into one with shaddah is called this.
Replacing one letter with another, as in "istabara" from s-b-r, is called this.
In "ittasala" from w-s-l, the waw changed into this letter.
In "istabara" from s-b-r, the ta' of Form VIII changed into this letter.
In "izdahama" from z-h-m, the ta' of Form VIII changed into this letter.
"Qala" was originally this, before its waw became alif.
"Mizan" (scale) was originally this, before its waw became ya'.
The present tense of "wa'ada" drops its waw: this.
The command of "wa'ada".
The command of "waqa" (to protect), a single letter with ha' of pause.
The pattern of an intensive doer, like "ghaffar".
The intensive pattern of "ghafur" and "sabur".
A describing word that lasts, like "hasan" or "karim", is called this.
The masdar of a single act, like "jalsah" (one sitting).
The masdar of a manner of doing, like "jilsah" (a way of sitting).
A masdar that begins with mim, like "maw'id".
The masdar made by adding -iyyah, like "insaniyyah".
The plural of a plural is called this.
The broken plural patterns for 3 to 10 are called this.
The four patterns of jam' al-qillah.
The ultimate plural pattern, like "masajid" and "masabih".
Nouns on that pattern take this case behaviour.
The famous poem on verb patterns by Ibn Malik رحمة الله عليه.
The well-known modern teaching book of sarf by Ahmad al-Hamalawi رحمة الله عليه.
The classic beginners' book of sarf in the Ottoman and South Asian madrasahs, "The Foundation".
The book of sarf by Ibn al-Hajib رحمة الله عليه.
The ism al-fa'il of "rama".
The nisbah (relative adjective) of "Quraysh".
The broken plural pattern of "kitab" (kutub).
The broken plural pattern of "rajul" (rijal).

Two consonants without a vowel meeting is avoided; this is called this.
The ism al-fa'il of "qala".
The ism al-maf'ul of "qala".
The ism al-maf'ul of "rama".
The ism al-maf'ul of "da'a" (to call).
The diminutive of "kitab".
The relative adjective (nisbah) of "Makkah".
